tagline: Prism OS — the operating system for smart glasses.
doneDefinition: Every piece carries two consecutive PASS verdicts from two different fresh critics; the coherence integrator signs off on the whole system; the web apps runtime actually runs a third-party app; the developer platform is real; the dashboard shows N/N passed.
passRule: PASS requires, twice consecutively from two DIFFERENT fresh critics: ours ranked first overall, or tied-first with zero named gaps. One pass is luck. Two is real.

antiStall.ratchet: Below 75 total, score must climb >=5 per round. Two rounds under +5 -> discard the builder's approach and respawn with a different one.
antiStall.rebuild: 4 fails with <10 total improvement -> delete the piece and rebuild from scratch.
antiStall.sweep: Same gap category named on >=3 pieces -> freeze new rounds, run ONE sweep agent across every piece.
antiStall.noSilentDescope: Anything that cannot be done goes under 'blocked' with a reason. Dropping it quietly is the worst available outcome.

rootCauses: The loop never looped: 10 of 16 pieces sat at FAIL with no builder ever sent back.
Focus discipline named the biggest gap on 9 pieces across 11 verdicts, fixed on none.
Engineering tokens ('tabular', 'prism-ease · 260ms') shipped in user-visible copy on 5 pieces.
Web Apps was a picture of a platform: zero iframe, zero sandbox, zero manifest, zero postMessage.
The Meta developer platform was in scope and was silently dropped.
328MB of screenshots across 411 PNGs; nothing committed for 8 hours of work.

countermeasures: tools/probe.mjs is now an enforcing GATE (exit 1 on violation), not a reporter. It fails the build on dev chrome inside the stage, engineering tokens in rendered text, stage overflow, unhonored reduced motion, unnamed focusables, and any console or page error.
os/shared/lab.js moves every developer control OUT of the 600x600 stage into a fixed rail, and drives all five edge states from the URL so critics can screenshot them.
os/shared/lab.js also paints a world layer behind the glass, so material honesty is judgeable instead of assumed.
The critic's disqualification rule lives in .claude/agents/prism-critic.md frontmatter, so it survives a spawn prompt that forgets to repeat it.
No piece is ever left at FAIL without a live builder on it.

waves.name: foundation
waves.rationale: The visual, motion, and sensory language every other piece inherits. Nothing else may start until these pass, because a wrong foundation is what produced a 55/90 plateau last time.

waves.name: shell
waves.rationale: Boot, home, window management, input, and text entry. Every app surface depends on these interaction primitives.

waves.name: system surfaces
waves.rationale: Cross-cutting system UI. Notifications, assistant, search, privacy, settings, accessibility. Apps assume these exist.

waves.name: first-party apps
waves.rationale: The apps that prove the shell works. Each is an independent surface a critic can rank alone.

waves.name: platform
waves.rationale: The third-party story that was silently dropped last time: a runtime that actually runs foreign code, a permission broker that actually enforces, a catalog, an SDK, a simulator, and the out-of-box flow that ties it together.

pieces.name: foundation & materials
pieces.surface: A single real surface that demonstrates glass over world, type scale, and controls in use — not a token catalog.
pieces.verdict: FAIL r2 (tie at 71 with named gaps)
pieces.gap: Density ladder inverted in rendered pixels: Glass transmits 0.53 of world luminance, Sheet transmits 1.04 — backwards. On Outdoor the streetlamp reads as a hard shape through Sheet, whose own caption says the world stays as colour not shapes, while Glass erases it and reads as a sunglasses tint. Also: .ctl .btn and .toggle are hardcoded px and do not scale with --a11y-scale, ending up half the size of the copy at scale 2.
pieces.ratchet: under 75 and went backwards (74 to 71) — one round under +5, round 3 must reach 78 or the approach gets discarded

pieces.name: motion & transition language
pieces.surface: Every transition the OS uses, shown on real surfaces: rise, sheet, dismiss, handoff, interrupt.
pieces.verdict: FAIL r1 (tie at 73 with named gaps)
pieces.gap: resize() measures the post-mutation height before cancelling the in-flight height animation, so h1-h0 < 1px, the guard returns early, and interruption is ignored — then a 61px single-frame snap. Plus: card hover feedback is dead because the enter animation holds fill:'both'; and advance() matches the leaving card, so two fast dismisses silently eat a message.
pieces.ratchet: under 75 — round 2 must reach 78 or higher

pieces.name: spatial audio & haptics
pieces.surface: Spatial audio placement and the haptic vocabulary, made visible and audible.
pieces.verdict: PASS r1 (1 of 2), r2 gate green, awaiting second critic
pieces.gap: Bearing readout collides with the compass-rose "behind" label and the source orb in every cue state. Also: at text scale 1.6 the column overflows 676 vs 556 and clips "Confirm" and "Capture" out of reach.

pieces.name: boot & recovery

blocked.item: Sub-agent reasoning effort = medium, set via .claude/agents/*.md frontmatter
blocked.detail: The four agent definitions exist on disk with `model: opus` and `effort: medium`. The Claude Code harness registers .claude/agents/*.md at SESSION START, so definitions authored mid-session are not selectable as subagent_type in this run — a spawn with subagent_type 'prism-builder' errors with 'Agent type not found'.
blocked.workaround: Spawning the generic agent with an explicit model override (verified: reports claude-opus-5) and prepending the full role definition — including the critic's disqualification rule — to every spawn prompt. Behaviour matches the definitions; only the effort knob is not settable per-spawn.
blocked.residual: Reasoning effort cannot be pinned to medium from inside this session and is not introspectable by a subagent. The frontmatter takes effect on the next session start. Verified via throwaway spawn: model is claude-opus-5; effort was not determinable.
blocked.resolution: Session restarted, so .claude/agents/*.md registered. prism-builder / prism-critic / prism-sweep / prism-integrator are now selectable as subagent_type, carrying `model: opus` + `effort: medium` from frontmatter. No per-spawn override needed; the workaround is retired.

blocked.item: Opus 5 session rate limit halted all three wave-0 builders mid-run
blocked.detail: All three wave-0 builders terminated with HTTP 429 rate_limit ('You've hit your session limit', model claude-opus-5). 00-foundation and 17-audio-haptics had already written complete files; 16-motion had written nothing.
blocked.resolution: Limit reset. Both written files were re-gated on resume and both exit 0 (GATE: PASS), so no work was lost. 16-motion respawned from scratch.

blocked.item: Opus 5 session rate limit — second hit, killed all three live agents
blocked.status: RESOLVED, but recurring; recorded as a known operating constraint
blocked.detail: All three agents (00-foundation r2 builder, 17-audio-haptics r2 builder, 16-motion critic) terminated with HTTP 429 rate_limit, reset 12:10pm Asia/Calcutta. Three parallel Opus agents exhaust the session limit in roughly 30-40 minutes of work.
blocked.resolution: Both builders had already written complete files before dying — the Write lands atomically, so no work was lost either time. Each file failed exactly one gate check (00-foundation: stage overflow 648>600; 17-audio-haptics: glyphs in the reticle rest zone) because neither builder reached its self-verify step. Both respawned to finish from the current file state rather than from scratch. The 16-motion critic had written no verdict and was respawned clean.
blocked.mitigation: Every killed agent's partial output is re-gated by the orchestrator before it is trusted or discarded. The gate is what makes an interrupted run recoverable instead of a loss.

blocked.item: Opus 5 session rate limit — third hit, killed all three live agents
blocked.detail: Rate limit fired again at ~12:50pm Asia/Calcutta with reset at 5:30pm. Killed 'Fix 00-foundation r3' (had read nothing yet), 'Judge 17-audio-haptics r2' (no verdict written), and 'Fix 16-motion r2' (died at the write boundary, mid-sentence on 'Now I'll rewrite the piece'). Working tree was clean on resume, so 16-motion had written nothing — unlike hits #1 and #2, no partial file to re-gate.
blocked.resolution: Waited out the reset, re-gated disk state (git status clean, no source file touched), respawned all three. Standing protocol confirmed for a third time: on any kill, check git status and re-run the probe gate on every file a dead agent could have written before trusting or discarding it.

blocked.item: Static server on :4310 died between sessions, silently failing every spawned agent
blocked.detail: The `python3 -m http.server 4310` process did not survive the process restart. Three agents spawned against a dead server: curl returned connection-refused (exit 7) and no agent could load a page or run the probe. They left two empty probe dirs and no verdicts. The failure is silent from the orchestrator's side — the agents just stop with no completion record.
blocked.resolution: Restarted detached (pid confirmed via pgrep, /index.html returns 200) and verified it survives the background-task completion notification. Every spawn prompt now carries the curl health check plus the restart command, so an agent repairs a dead server itself instead of dying on it. Server is re-verified before each wave and after any process restart.

blocked.item: Rate-limit hit #4 on the Opus 5 session quota
blocked.detail: Sub-agent spawns unavailable until the 22:50 Asia/Calcutta reset. No builder or critic can run in the interim.
blocked.workaround: Orchestrator-side work continues in the main session: the Web Apps surface was rebuilt, probed and committed without a sub-agent. Critics are queued for the reset.
blocked.residual: Verdicts for 00-foundation r3, 16-motion r2, 17-audio-haptics r2 and 12-webapps r1 are all waiting on the reset.

blocked.detail: core.js converts the pointer to stage-local coordinates by dividing by state.scale, then passes those to document.elementFromPoint(), which expects viewport coordinates. Under any stage transform the hit test resolves to the wrong element or to none, so .gaze-focus never lands where the wearer is looking.
blocked.workaround: Section 10 freezes core.js, so the correction lives in hardenGaze() in os/shared/lab.js: a viewport-space hit test registered after core's own listener, which therefore has the last word on .gaze-focus. Every piece already calls hardenGaze, so the fix is systemic rather than per-piece. Verified: .gaze-focus now settles on the element under the gaze at 310% text scale.
blocked.residual: The ACTIVATION path is still wrong. core.js pointerdown calls focused.click() against its own mis-resolved element, so a click can fire on an element the wearer was not looking at. The lab-side listener corrects the highlight, not the dispatch. Fixing it needs either an edit to frozen core.js or a capture-phase interceptor that swallows core's pointerdown, and neither is in scope without permission to touch the frozen file. Recorded here rather than dropped.

deviations.item: Reticle rest-zone rule not enforced above 100% text scale
deviations.detail: The probe's reticle rest-point check runs at default scale only. The builder self-reported a residual: at exactly 200-240% text the bearing line passes through the stage-centre rest point.
deviations.decision: Left for the critic to judge rather than gated. The rest-zone rule is a proxy for the real requirement, which is that the reticle must never occlude a glyph; the systemic fix already composites it as a hollow ring that stays invisible until gaze. Extending an absolute centre-clear rule to 240% text would force layouts to keep a hole in the middle of the screen at the exact scale where space is scarcest.
deviations.risk: If a critic names it, it becomes a real gap and gets fixed.
